# aif-plan Task and Plan Format

## Plan File Naming

`workflow.plan_id_format` (config) controls the full/ultra plan identifier shape:

| Value        | Full shape / Ultra shape                                    | Notes                                                                 |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `slug`       | `paths.plans/<stem>.md` / `paths.plans/<stem>/index.md`     | Default. Derived from branch name (or description slug in no-git mode).|
| `timestamp`  | (reserved; behaves like `slug`)                             | Reserved value. Currently falls back to `slug` with an `INFO` log.    |
| `uuid`       | (reserved; behaves like `slug`)                             | Reserved value. Currently falls back to `slug` with an `INFO` log.    |
| `sequential` | `paths.plans/<NNNN>_<stem>.md` / `paths.plans/<NNNN>_<stem>/index.md` | `NNNN = max(existing 4-digit prefix across full files and directories whose `index.md` has the exact ultra marker) + 1`; other numbered directories are ignored; empty plans start at `0001`; capped at `9999`. Deleting the highest-numbered plan can free that number for reuse. Force-disabled under `HANDOFF_BRANCH_PREPARED=1`. |

Branch names always remain `<branch_prefix><slug>` regardless of the format вЂ”
the prefix lives only on the full-plan filename or ultra directory. Fast plans
(`paths.plan`) and fix plans (`paths.fix_plan`) are single files and ignore
`plan_id_format`.

This file defines the fast/full single-file format. For the ultra bundle,
including `index.md`, phase files, detail gates, and consumer rules, read
`ULTRA-FORMAT.md`.

## Plan File Template

```markdown
<!-- handoff:task:<HANDOFF_TASK_ID> -->
<!-- в†‘ First line: only when HANDOFF_MODE=1 and HANDOFF_TASK_ID is non-empty -->

# Implementation Plan: [Feature Name]

Branch: [current branch or "none"]
Created: [date]

## Original Request
<!-- Required when the user explicitly supplied a planning request. Omit only when the plan was created solely from RESEARCH.md without an explicit user request. Preserve the request after only recognized command tokens in command positions are removed and only outer whitespace is trimmed; do not translate, summarize, normalize, or rewrite it. -->
[exact user-provided planning request]

## Settings
- Testing: yes/no
- Logging: verbose/standard/minimal
- Docs: yes/no  # yes => mandatory docs checkpoint in $aif-implement, no/unset => WARN [docs] only
- Commit strategy: incremental/incremental-at-end/single-commit  # how commits are structured
- Development methodology: implementation-first/tdd  # implementation-first or test-driven development
- TDD granularity: task-based/feature-based  # only shown when Development methodology: tdd

## Roadmap Linkage (optional)
<!-- Only when .ai-factory/ROADMAP.md exists -->
Milestone: "[milestone name from ROADMAP.md]"  # or "none"
Also completes: "[additional selected milestone]"  # optional; repeat once per remaining milestone
Rationale: [1 short sentence]

## Research Context (optional)
<!-- Only when a selected legacy or ultra-bundle RESEARCH.md influenced this plan, copy/paste the relevant Active Summary here -->
Source: `.ai-factory/RESEARCH.md` (Active Summary, Updated: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, SHA256: <active-summary-sha256>)
<!-- Required when any RESEARCH.md content influenced this plan. Replace the example source with the exact selected file, including research/<slug>/RESEARCH.md for ultra research. The copied context is the committed requirements snapshot; downstream skills use the live source file only to warn about revision drift. -->

Goal:
Constraints:
Decisions:
Open questions:

## Requirements Reconciliation
<!-- Include when multiple authoritative sources constrain behavior, a conflict was resolved, independent behavior dimensions exist, or a representative repository artifact is required. Keep this exact heading. -->
Authority: [declared source priority, or "none declared"]

| Decision / supported combination | Source path and section | Verification evidence |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------|
| [material rule or combination] | `[path]` вЂ” [section] | [test, command, or manual check] |

## Tasks

### Phase 1: Setup
- [ ] Task 1: [description]
- [ ] Task 2: [description]

### Phase 2: Core Implementation
- [ ] Task 3: [description] (depends on 1, 2)
- [ ] Task 4: [description]

### Phase 3: Integration
- [ ] Task 5: [description] (depends on 3, 4)
```

Keep `## Settings` and the `Commit strategy:`, `Development methodology:`,
and `TDD granularity:` labels exactly as shown in every artifact language;
these are untranslated control tokens read by `$aif-implement`. Keep values
canonical and untranslated as well.

Render exactly one commit layout in a generated plan; never combine these
formats. The common template above contains tasks and settings, but not the
optional commit layout:

- For `workflow.plan_structure: classic`, include a `## Commit Plan` section
  with ordered task ranges and messages when commits are planned. Classic is
  the only format that uses this section.
- For `workflow.plan_structure: task-based`, omit `## Commit Plan` and add
  explicit commit tasks to `## Tasks`. Put the stable marker on its own line
  immediately before the actual task checkbox; never create a checkbox for the
  marker itself.

**Classic layout example (`incremental`):**

```markdown
## Commit Plan
- **Commit 1** (after tasks 1-3): "feat: add user model"
- **Commit 2** (after tasks 4-6): "feat: implement auth service"
```

**Task-based layout example:**

```markdown
## Tasks
### Phase 1: User Authentication System
- [ ] Task 1: Implement user service
- [ ] Task 2: Write unit tests for user service (depends on 1)
- [ ] Task 3: Document user service API (depends on 1)
<!-- aif:task-kind:commit -->
- [ ] Task 4: Commit changes with message "feat: implement user service" (depends on 1,2,3)
```

For `incremental`, place each marked commit task after its related work. For
`incremental-at-end`, place all marked commit tasks after implementation tasks,
one per planned group. For `single-commit`, add one marked final task depending
on all work. TDD granularity changes test/implementation ordering only; every
commit task still uses the same marker placement and grouping contract.

For classic plans, `Commit strategy: incremental-at-end` means list each logical
group in `## Commit Plan` as deferred until all implementation/test/documentation
tasks are complete. Keep the task-range syntax and make deferral explicit, e.g.
`- **Commit 1** (after tasks 1-3; defer until all tasks complete): "feat: ..."`
`$aif-implement` commits those groups in listed order only during finalization.
`single-commit` means exactly one deferred group covering all
implementation/test/documentation tasks. Neither deferred strategy may commit
at an intermediate task-range boundary.

For either deferred strategy with `Docs: yes`, include a final documentation
task for the mandatory `$aif-docs` checkpoint and give it explicit `Files:`
hints. In classic `incremental-at-end`, place this task in a dedicated final
commit group; in `single-commit`, include it in the one group. In task-based
plans, the corresponding commit task must depend on the documentation task.
After `$aif-docs`, `$aif-implement` verifies every changed documentation
path/hunk is covered by that task's hints and selected group. If the diff
escapes the reserved scope or overlaps another group ambiguously, stop before
committing and ask the user to adjust the plan grouping.

## TaskCreate Example

```text
TaskCreate:
  subject: "Implement user login endpoint"
  description: |
    Create POST /api/auth/login endpoint that:
    - Accepts email and password
    - Validates credentials against database
    - Returns JWT token on success
    - Returns 401 on invalid credentials

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log function entry with request context
    - Log validation result (pass/fail with reasons)
    - Log external service calls and responses
    - Log any errors with full context
    - Use format: [ServiceName.method] message {data}
    - Use log levels (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR)

    Files: src/api/auth/login.ts, src/services/auth.ts

    REQUIREMENT EVIDENCE (when the Requirements Reconciliation Gate applies):
    - Source: `docs/auth.md` вЂ” Login contract
    - Supported combinations: valid/invalid credentials Г— active/disabled user
    - Verification: exercise each supported combination through POST /api/auth/login
  activeForm: "Implementing login endpoint"
```

## Logging Requirements Checklist

Every task description should specify:
- What to log: inputs, outputs, state changes, errors
- Where to log: key checkpoints and external boundaries
- Levels: DEBUG for verbose flow, INFO for major events, ERROR for failures
- Control: environment-driven (`LOG_LEVEL` or `DEBUG`)
- Safety: production log level can be reduced without code edits

Never create tasks without logging instructions.

## TDD Task Pattern Examples

**Task-Based TDD Pattern:**
```text
TaskCreate:
  subject: "Write failing unit test for user login"
  description: |
    Write a unit test for the user login functionality that:
    - Tests successful login with valid credentials
    - Tests failed login with invalid credentials
    - Tests edge cases (empty email, missing password)

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log test file creation
    - Log test execution results
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for test creation, DEBUG for test details

    Files: tests/auth/login.test.ts
  activeForm: "Writing failing unit test for user login"

TaskCreate:
  subject: "Implement user login to make test pass"
  description: |
    Implement the user login functionality to pass the login test:
    - Implement authentication logic
    - Handle valid credentials
    - Handle invalid credentials with appropriate error response
    - Ensure test from previous task passes

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log implementation progress
    - Log test validation
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for progress, DEBUG for validation

    Files: src/services/auth.ts
  activeForm: "Implementing user login"
```

**Feature-Based TDD Pattern:**
```text
TaskCreate:
  subject: "Write failing unit tests for user authentication"
  description: |
    Write unit tests for the user authentication feature:
    - Test user login functionality
    - Test user registration functionality
    - Test password validation
    - Test session management

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log test file creation
    - Log test suite composition
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for test creation, DEBUG for test details

    Files: tests/auth/user-auth.test.ts
  activeForm: "Writing failing unit tests for user authentication"

TaskCreate:
  subject: "Implement user authentication to make tests pass"
  description: |
    Implement the user authentication feature to pass all tests:
    - Implement user login
    - Implement user registration
    - Implement password validation
    - Implement session management

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log implementation progress
    - Log test validation
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for progress, DEBUG for validation

    Files: src/services/auth.ts, src/middleware/auth.ts
  activeForm: "Implementing user authentication"
```
# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ core/        в†ђ helpers with no knowledge of features
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ format/  в†ђ NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ money/   в†ђ arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ utils/   в†ђ Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ domain/      в†ђ pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ model/
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ data/        в†ђ everything that talks to the outside world
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ remote/  в†ђ FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/ в†ђ repository implementations and DTO в†’ domain converters
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ feature/<feature>/<screen>/ в†ђ screens, see screen.md
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ root/        в†ђ the navigation stack of the app
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ ui/          в†ђ AppTheme, Strings
в””в”Ђв”Ђ di/          в†ђ AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature в†’ domain в†ђ data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only вЂ” never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.

# FX Rates

## Purpose and current scope

A Kotlin Multiplatform currency-rate viewer. The Android app displays ECB reference rates obtained
through Frankfurter. Android and iOS targets share the application code; there is currently no iOS
host application.

The implemented `RatesList` screen loads rates against USD, supports refresh and filtering by
currency code or name, and displays loading, error, empty-search and content states. Rows show the
latest rate and a change from the previous available business day. Selecting a currency opens a
detail screen showing the latest dated rate, available history in the last 30 UTC calendar days,
and the absolute and percentage change across that history.

## Stack

| Concern | Existing choice |
|---------|-----------------|
| Language and shared code | Kotlin Multiplatform |
| UI | Compose Multiplatform, Material 3 |
| Components and navigation | Decompose, Essenty lifecycle |
| Screen state and effects | MVIKotlin, coroutines and Flow |
| Dependency injection | kotlin-inject with KSP and assisted component factories |
| Networking | Ktor client; OkHttp on Android and Darwin on iOS |
| Serialization and dates | kotlinx.serialization, kotlinx.datetime |
| Decimal arithmetic | `com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.BigDecimal` |
| Tests | kotest `FunSpec`, coroutine test dispatchers, hand-written repository fakes |
| Build and checks | Gradle wrapper, JDK 21, Android Gradle Plugin, detekt |
| Persistence and backend | No local database, ORM or repository-owned server |

Dependency versions and Android SDK levels are defined in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. Toolchain
requirements and commands are documented in `README.md` and `docs/commands.md`.

## Code organization and boundaries

- `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/` holds application logic and UI.
- `shared/src/commonTest/kotlin/com/fxrates/` holds tests and reusable fakes.
- `shared/src/androidMain/` and `shared/src/iosMain/` hold HTTP-engine platform glue.
- `androidApp/` hosts the root component through `MainActivity`.
- `core/` contains reusable formatting, rate arithmetic and resource utilities.
- `domain/` contains models and repository interfaces, independent of Ktor and Compose.
- `data/` contains the API client, DTOs, converters and repository implementations.
- `feature/<feature>/<screen>/` contains each screen's Store, Reducer, Executor, StoreFactory,
  UI models, UiState, converter, component, content and previews.
- `root/` owns the navigation stack; `ui/` owns shared strings and theme; `di/` wires dependencies.

Dependencies follow `feature -> domain <- data`. The composition root binds implementations to
interfaces. Screens access repository interfaces and domain models; DTO conversion belongs in the
data layer. `RatesList` is the reference screen for subsequent work.

## Architecture

Pattern: Domain ports and data adapters, with MVI screens.

See the local [architecture guide](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the existing folder structure, dependency
rules, data flow and examples. The shared architecture and screen documents remain authoritative.

## Data and execution patterns

The configured API base is `https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`. `FrankfurterApi` exposes currency names
and a rate time series. `RatesRepositoryImpl` requests a seven-calendar-day lookback and currency
names concurrently for the list, then delegates conversion to `RatesConverter`. The detail read
requests the inclusive 30-day UTC window for the selected currency. Calendar windows can contain
fewer observations because reference rates are available on business days.

Store state holds domain models and `Resource` values. Intent handling dispatches messages,
publishes labels or forwards actions; actions carry everything their side effects need. Repository
operations use `resourceFlow`, which emits loading and data/error states and rethrows cancellation.
Reducers are pure. UiState converters prepare display values using `NumberFormatter` and
`RateChangeCalculator`; composables draw the prepared state. Labels become component callbacks,
and the root owns navigation.

## Project rules

`AGENTS.md` is the entry point for mandatory repository rules. Read the relevant documents before
changing their areas:

- `docs/architecture.md`: modules, dependency directions, data conversion and dependency injection.
- `docs/screen.md`: screen files, MVI responsibilities, navigation and screen tests.
- `docs/conventions.md`: Kotlin, decimal arithmetic, Compose, naming and testing conventions.
- `docs/commands.md`: build, test, static analysis and completion requirements.

These documents govern setup-generated context too. Existing deviations are debt, not permission
to weaken a rule. Additional application dependencies require a written reason.

Rates and changes use `BigDecimal`; a zero starting rate leaves the percentage undefined while
preserving the absolute change.

## Verification

The required repository check is:

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug
```

For screen changes, also launch the app and inspect the changed screen, including loading and
error states, as required by `docs/commands.md`.

# Architecture: Domain ports and MVI screens

## Overview

This is a local AI Factory guide to the existing application. The shared architectural authority
is [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md), together with [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[screen rules](../docs/screen.md) and [code conventions](../docs/conventions.md).

The application separates domain contracts from data adapters and screen presentation. Its central
dependency rule is `feature -> domain <- data`. MVIKotlin orchestrates screen state and effects,
Decompose owns components and navigation, and kotlin-inject wires implementations at the composition
root. This document describes those existing boundaries; it does not introduce another layer or
require a folder migration.

## Decision rationale

- The product is a small currency-rate viewer with list and detail screens.
- Kotlin Multiplatform shares application code and UI; an Android host supplies the entry point.
- Domain repository interfaces isolate screens from HTTP and allow tests to use hand-written fakes.
- Existing reusable formatting and rate arithmetic keep presentation consistent across screens.

## Modules and folders

```text
androidApp/src/main/kotlin/com/fxrates/app/
    MainActivity.kt                 Android host
shared/src/
    commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/
        core/
            format/                 NumberFormatter
            money/                  RateChange, RateChangeCalculator
            utils/                  Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
        domain/
            model/                  CurrencyRate, DatedRate
            repository/             RatesRepository interface
        data/
            remote/                 FrankfurterApi, HTTP configuration and DTOs
            repository/             RatesRepositoryImpl, RatesConverter
        feature/rates/list/         Reference screen, including mvi/ and model/
        feature/rates/detail/       Detail screen, including mvi/ and model/
        root/                       RootUiComponent, RootUiContent
        ui/                         Strings and theme/
        di/                         AppComponent and createRootComponent
    commonTest/kotlin/com/fxrates/   Tests mirroring production packages; testing/ holds fakes
    androidMain/                    OkHttp engine glue
    iosMain/                        Darwin engine glue
```

`:shared` targets Android, iOS arm64 and the iOS arm64 simulator. The iOS targets guard common-code
portability; there is no iOS host app. Application logic belongs in `commonMain`, tests in
`commonTest`, and platform source sets supply HTTP-engine glue. The Android module only hosts the
root component.

## Dependency rules

```text
feature  ---> domain <--- data
   |                       |
   +----> core <-----------+

di wires domain interfaces to data implementations and creates component factories.
root composes screen components and owns the navigation stack.
ui supplies shared strings and theme values to presentation.
```

- `domain` contains models and repository interfaces. It uses shared decimal and date types,
  and has no Ktor, Compose or DTO dependencies.
- `data` implements domain repositories and owns remote access and DTO-to-domain conversion.
- `feature` works through domain contracts. A screen never imports a DTO, API client or HTTP client.
- `core` provides reusable helpers without feature dependencies. Reuse `NumberFormatter` and
  `RateChangeCalculator` for their respective responsibilities.
- `di/AppComponent.kt` is the composition root. Constructor dependencies use `@Inject`; interface
  bindings use `@Provides`, and long-lived clients and repositories use `@AppScope`.
- Component factories mark `ComponentContext`, screen arguments and callbacks as `@Assisted`.

These are package boundaries inside the existing shared Gradle module, not additional Gradle modules.

## Screen communication

Use the file layout in [docs/screen.md](../docs/screen.md) and `feature/rates/list/` for each new screen.
The Store contains nested Intent, Action, Message, Label and State types. The Reducer, Executor and
StoreFactory have separate responsibilities.

1. Compose calls an action on the abstract UiComponent contract.
2. The component accepts a Store Intent.
3. `executeIntent` reads state as needed and dispatches a message, publishes a label or forwards
   an Action. Actions carry all values needed by their effects.
4. `executeAction` starts effects without reading Store state. Repository calls flow through
   `resourceFlow`, then dispatch Messages. Cancellation propagates; ordinary failures become
   `Resource.Error`.
5. The pure Reducer returns a copied State containing domain values and resource status.
6. The UiStateConverter derives display models, strings and flags. Formatting goes through
   `NumberFormatter`; rate arithmetic goes through `core/money`.
7. The component exposes converted state as a `StateFlow`. Compose draws this prepared state.

Initial loading uses a `SimpleBootstrapper` Action in the StoreFactory. UiState and its UI models
are immutable. Shared strings live in `ui/Strings.kt`; spacing and semantic colors come from the
theme, and typography comes from `MaterialTheme`.

Navigation follows a separate path: a Store Label becomes a component callback, and the root
changes the Decompose stack. Serializable configurations carry identifiers rather than domain
models. Back handling belongs to the root stack. Selecting a list row pushes a detail configuration
with base and currency identifiers; the detail screen loads its own history.

## Data communication

`RatesRepository` is the domain port; `RatesRepositoryImpl` is the data adapter. The implementation
fetches currency names and a seven-calendar-day time series concurrently through `FrankfurterApi`,
using an injected clock to choose the start date. `RatesConverter` selects the latest two available
dates, maps values to domain models, falls back to a code for an unknown currency name, and sorts
the result by code. The history read uses the injected clock for an inclusive 30-day UTC window,
selects the requested currency, and returns available observations newest first.

The API base is configured in `data/remote/HttpClientFactory.kt`. Ktor handles JSON and unsuccessful
HTTP responses; platform implementations choose OkHttp or Darwin. Business-day observations can
leave fewer data points than the calendar window. There is no local database or persistent cache.

An additional read from this data source belongs on the existing repository and API client. Keep
DTO conversion in the data layer and bind interface implementations in `AppComponent`.

## Code examples

These excerpts illustrate existing boundaries; they are not additional application files.

### Domain contract

From `domain/repository/RatesRepository.kt`:

```kotlin
interface RatesRepository {

    suspend fun getLatestRates(base: String): List<CurrencyRate>

    suspend fun getRateHistory(base: String, code: String): List<DatedRate>

}
```

Both production adapters and test fakes implement this contract; screens depend on the interface.

### Action-driven effect

From `feature/rates/list/mvi/RatesListExecutor.kt`:

```kotlin
private fun loadRates(action: Action.LoadRates) {
    resourceFlow { repository.getLatestRates(base = action.base) }
        .onEach { rates -> dispatch(Message.UpdateRates(rates)) }
        .launchIn(scope)
}
```

The Action supplies the base currency. Loading and failures become resource values that reach the
Reducer through Messages.

## Key principles

Follow the fixed stack and the shared repository rules. Keep effects in Executors, conversion in
converters, arithmetic in `core/money`, formatting in `NumberFormatter`, and navigation in the root.
Use named lambda parameters, explicit lambda invocation and sealed classes as documented in
[docs/conventions.md](../docs/conventions.md).

Rates and derived monetary values use `BigDecimal`. Percentage change is relative to the previous
rate and is undefined when that rate is zero; the absolute change remains available.

# FX Rates

## Purpose and current scope

A Kotlin Multiplatform currency-rate viewer. The Android app displays ECB reference rates obtained
through Frankfurter. Android and iOS targets share the application code; there is currently no iOS
host application.

The implemented `RatesList` screen loads rates against USD, supports refresh and filtering by
currency code or name, and displays loading, error, empty-search and content states. Rows show the
latest rate and a change from the previous available business day. Selecting a currency opens a
detail screen showing the latest dated rate, available history in the last 30 UTC calendar days,
and the absolute and percentage change across that history.

## Stack

| Concern | Existing choice |
|---------|-----------------|
| Language and shared code | Kotlin Multiplatform |
| UI | Compose Multiplatform, Material 3 |
| Components and navigation | Decompose, Essenty lifecycle |
| Screen state and effects | MVIKotlin, coroutines and Flow |
| Dependency injection | kotlin-inject with KSP and assisted component factories |
| Networking | Ktor client; OkHttp on Android and Darwin on iOS |
| Serialization and dates | kotlinx.serialization, kotlinx.datetime |
| Decimal arithmetic | `com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.BigDecimal` |
| Tests | kotest `FunSpec`, coroutine test dispatchers, hand-written repository fakes |
| Build and checks | Gradle wrapper, JDK 21, Android Gradle Plugin, detekt |
| Persistence and backend | No local database, ORM or repository-owned server |

Dependency versions and Android SDK levels are defined in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. Toolchain
requirements and commands are documented in `README.md` and `docs/commands.md`.

## Code organization and boundaries

- `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/` holds application logic and UI.
- `shared/src/commonTest/kotlin/com/fxrates/` holds tests and reusable fakes.
- `shared/src/androidMain/` and `shared/src/iosMain/` hold HTTP-engine platform glue.
- `androidApp/` hosts the root component through `MainActivity`.
- `core/` contains reusable formatting, rate arithmetic and resource utilities.
- `domain/` contains models and repository interfaces, independent of Ktor and Compose.
- `data/` contains the API client, DTOs, converters and repository implementations.
- `feature/<feature>/<screen>/` contains each screen's Store, Reducer, Executor, StoreFactory,
  UI models, UiState, converter, component, content and previews.
- `root/` owns the navigation stack; `ui/` owns shared strings and theme; `di/` wires dependencies.

Dependencies follow `feature -> domain <- data`. The composition root binds implementations to
interfaces. Screens access repository interfaces and domain models; DTO conversion belongs in the
data layer. `RatesList` is the reference screen for subsequent work.

## Architecture

Pattern: Domain ports and data adapters, with MVI screens.

See the local [architecture guide](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the existing folder structure, dependency
rules, data flow and examples. The shared architecture and screen documents remain authoritative.

## Data and execution patterns

The configured API base is `https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`. `FrankfurterApi` exposes currency names
and a rate time series. `RatesRepositoryImpl` requests a seven-calendar-day lookback and currency
names concurrently for the list, then delegates conversion to `RatesConverter`. The detail read
requests the inclusive 30-day UTC window for the selected currency. Calendar windows can contain
fewer observations because reference rates are available on business days.

Store state holds domain models and `Resource` values. Intent handling dispatches messages,
publishes labels or forwards actions; actions carry everything their side effects need. Repository
operations use `resourceFlow`, which emits loading and data/error states and rethrows cancellation.
Reducers are pure. UiState converters prepare display values using `NumberFormatter` and
`RateChangeCalculator`; composables draw the prepared state. Labels become component callbacks,
and the root owns navigation.

changing their areas:

- `docs/architecture.md`: modules, dependency directions, data conversion and dependency injection.
- `docs/screen.md`: screen files, MVI responsibilities, navigation and screen tests.

These documents govern setup-generated context too. Existing deviations are debt, not permission

Rates and changes use `BigDecimal`; a zero starting rate leaves the percentage undefined while

these are untranslated control tokens read by `$aif-implement`. Keep values
canonical and untranslated as well.

Render exactly one commit layout in a generated plan; never combine these
formats. The common template above contains tasks and settings, but not the
optional commit layout:

- For `workflow.plan_structure: classic`, include a `## Commit Plan` section
  with ordered task ranges and messages when commits are planned. Classic is
  the only format that uses this section.
- For `workflow.plan_structure: task-based`, omit `## Commit Plan` and add
  explicit commit tasks to `## Tasks`. Put the stable marker on its own line
  immediately before the actual task checkbox; never create a checkbox for the
  marker itself.

**Classic layout example (`incremental`):**

```markdown
## Commit Plan
- **Commit 1** (after tasks 1-3): "feat: add user model"
- **Commit 2** (after tasks 4-6): "feat: implement auth service"
```

**Task-based layout example:**

```markdown
## Tasks
### Phase 1: User Authentication System
- [ ] Task 1: Implement user service
- [ ] Task 2: Write unit tests for user service (depends on 1)
- [ ] Task 3: Document user service API (depends on 1)
<!-- aif:task-kind:commit -->
- [ ] Task 4: Commit changes with message "feat: implement user service" (depends on 1,2,3)
```

For `incremental`, place each marked commit task after its related work. For
`incremental-at-end`, place all marked commit tasks after implementation tasks,
one per planned group. For `single-commit`, add one marked final task depending
on all work. TDD granularity changes test/implementation ordering only; every
commit task still uses the same marker placement and grouping contract.

For classic plans, `Commit strategy: incremental-at-end` means list each logical
group in `## Commit Plan` as deferred until all implementation/test/documentation
tasks are complete. Keep the task-range syntax and make deferral explicit, e.g.
`- **Commit 1** (after tasks 1-3; defer until all tasks complete): "feat: ..."`
`$aif-implement` commits those groups in listed order only during finalization.
`single-commit` means exactly one deferred group covering all
implementation/test/documentation tasks. Neither deferred strategy may commit
at an intermediate task-range boundary.

For either deferred strategy with `Docs: yes`, include a final documentation
task for the mandatory `$aif-docs` checkpoint and give it explicit `Files:`
hints. In classic `incremental-at-end`, place this task in a dedicated final
commit group; in `single-commit`, include it in the one group. In task-based
plans, the corresponding commit task must depend on the documentation task.
After `$aif-docs`, `$aif-implement` verifies every changed documentation
path/hunk is covered by that task's hints and selected group. If the diff
escapes the reserved scope or overlaps another group ambiguously, stop before
committing and ask the user to adjust the plan grouping.

## TaskCreate Example

```text
TaskCreate:
  subject: "Implement user login endpoint"
  description: |
    Create POST /api/auth/login endpoint that:
    - Accepts email and password
    - Validates credentials against database
    - Returns JWT token on success
    - Returns 401 on invalid credentials

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log function entry with request context
    - Log validation result (pass/fail with reasons)
    - Log external service calls and responses
    - Log any errors with full context
    - Use format: [ServiceName.method] message {data}
    - Use log levels (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR)

    Files: src/api/auth/login.ts, src/services/auth.ts

    REQUIREMENT EVIDENCE (when the Requirements Reconciliation Gate applies):
    - Source: `docs/auth.md` вЂ” Login contract
    - Supported combinations: valid/invalid credentials Г— active/disabled user
    - Verification: exercise each supported combination through POST /api/auth/login
  activeForm: "Implementing login endpoint"
```

## Logging Requirements Checklist

Every task description should specify:
- What to log: inputs, outputs, state changes, errors
- Where to log: key checkpoints and external boundaries
- Levels: DEBUG for verbose flow, INFO for major events, ERROR for failures
- Control: environment-driven (`LOG_LEVEL` or `DEBUG`)
- Safety: production log level can be reduced without code edits

Never create tasks without logging instructions.

## TDD Task Pattern Examples

**Task-Based TDD Pattern:**
```text
TaskCreate:
  subject: "Write failing unit test for user login"
  description: |
    Write a unit test for the user login functionality that:
    - Tests successful login with valid credentials
    - Tests failed login with invalid credentials
    - Tests edge cases (empty email, missing password)

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log test file creation
    - Log test execution results
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for test creation, DEBUG for test details

    Files: tests/auth/login.test.ts
  activeForm: "Writing failing unit test for user login"

TaskCreate:
  subject: "Implement user login to make test pass"
  description: |
    Implement the user login functionality to pass the login test:
    - Implement authentication logic
    - Handle valid credentials
    - Handle invalid credentials with appropriate error response
    - Ensure test from previous task passes

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log implementation progress
    - Log test validation
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for progress, DEBUG for validation

    Files: src/services/auth.ts
  activeForm: "Implementing user login"
```

**Feature-Based TDD Pattern:**
```text
TaskCreate:
  subject: "Write failing unit tests for user authentication"
  description: |
    Write unit tests for the user authentication feature:
    - Test user login functionality
    - Test user registration functionality
    - Test password validation
    - Test session management

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log test file creation
    - Log test suite composition
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for test creation, DEBUG for test details

    Files: tests/auth/user-auth.test.ts
  activeForm: "Writing failing unit tests for user authentication"

TaskCreate:
  subject: "Implement user authentication to make tests pass"
  description: |
    Implement the user authentication feature to pass all tests:
    - Implement user login
    - Implement user registration
    - Implement password validation
    - Implement session management

    LOGGING REQUIREMENTS:
    - Log implementation progress
    - Log test validation
    - Use format: [aif-plan.tdd] message {data}
    - Use log levels: INFO for progress, DEBUG for validation

  activeForm: "Implementing user authentication"
```

# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ core/        в†ђ helpers with no knowledge of features
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ format/  в†ђ NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ money/   в†ђ arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ utils/   в†ђ Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ domain/      в†ђ pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ model/
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ data/        в†ђ everything that talks to the outside world
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ remote/  в†ђ FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/ в†ђ repository implementations and DTO в†’ domain converters
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ feature/<feature>/<screen>/ в†ђ screens, see screen.md
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ root/        в†ђ the navigation stack of the app
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ ui/          в†ђ AppTheme, Strings
в””в”Ђв”Ђ di/          в†ђ AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature в†’ domain в†ђ data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only вЂ” never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.

package com.fxrates.feature.rates.detail

import com.fxrates.core.utils.Resource
import com.fxrates.domain.model.DatedRate
import com.fxrates.feature.rates.detail.RatesDetailUiState.Content
import com.fxrates.feature.rates.detail.mvi.RatesDetailStore
import com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.toBigDecimal
import io.kotest.core.spec.style.FunSpec
import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
import io.kotest.matchers.types.shouldBeInstanceOf
import kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate

class RatesDetailUiStateConverterTest : FunSpec({

    val converter = RatesDetailUiStateConverter()
    fun rate(day: Int, value: String) = DatedRate(LocalDate(2026, 11, day), value.toBigDecimal())
    fun state(vararg rates: DatedRate) = RatesDetailStore.State("USD", "EUR", Resource.Data(rates.toList()))

    test("history is ordered newest first with latest date and signed period change") {
        val ui = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "1"), rate(3, "1.25"), rate(2, "1.1")))
        val content = ui.content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()

        ui.title shouldBe "1 USD in EUR"
        content.latest shouldBe "1.2500"
        content.latestDate shouldBe "2026-11-03"
        content.items.map { item -> item.date } shouldBe listOf("2026-11-03", "2026-11-02", "2026-11-01")
        content.absoluteChange shouldBe "+0.2500"
        content.percentChange shouldBe "+25.00%"
    }

    test("an empty history is distinct from loading and error") {
        converter.createUiState(state()).content shouldBe Content.Empty
        converter.createUiState(RatesDetailStore.State("USD", "EUR")).content shouldBe Content.Loading
        converter.createUiState(RatesDetailStore.State("USD", "EUR", Resource.Error(Exception()))).content shouldBe
            Content.Error
    }

    test("a single observation has no period change") {
        val content = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "1.25"))).content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        content.latestDate shouldBe "2026-11-01"
        content.absoluteChange shouldBe null
        content.percentChange shouldBe null
    }

    test("a zero starting rate keeps the absolute change and leaves percent unavailable") {
        val content = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "0"), rate(2, "1")))
            .content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        content.absoluteChange shouldBe "+1.0000"
        content.percentChange shouldBe null
    }

    test("falling and rounded-zero changes are formatted correctly") {
        val falling = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "2"), rate(2, "1")))
            .content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        falling.absoluteChange shouldBe "-1.0000"
        falling.percentChange shouldBe "-50.00%"
        val rounded = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "1"), rate(2, "1.000001")))
            .content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        rounded.absoluteChange shouldBe "0.0000"
        rounded.percentChange shouldBe "0.00%"
    }

})

# Best Practices Guide

## Shared project skill-context

Before mode routing or work, read existing files relative to the current project root in this order (reuse them if already loaded):

1. `.ai-factory/skill-context/global-skill-context.md` вЂ” all bundled skills.
2. `.ai-factory/skill-context/aif-best-practices/SKILL.md` вЂ” this skill.

Missing files are skipped; an existing unreadable file stops dependent work with its path.
Precedence: individual > build (when applicable) > global > skill defaults; retain non-conflicting instructions and check all outputs against the effective rules.
These layers customize workflow; they do not replace the project's rules/architecture hierarchy or relax explicit requirements, ownership, scope, safety/privacy, validation, or approval boundaries. Report conflicts with those boundaries instead of overriding them.
`global` is a project-local layer, not home-directory configuration. Custom/extension skills do not automatically use it.

Universal code quality guidelines applicable to any language or framework.

**Context:** If `.ai-factory/ARCHITECTURE.md` exists, follow its folder structure, dependency rules, and module boundaries alongside these guidelines.

**Read `.ai-factory/skill-context/aif-best-practices/SKILL.md`** вЂ” MANDATORY if the file exists.

This file contains project-specific rules accumulated by `$aif-evolve` from patches,
codebase conventions, and tech-stack analysis. These rules are tailored to the current project.

**How to apply skill-context rules:**
- Treat them as **project-level overrides** for this skill's general instructions
- When a skill-context rule conflicts with a general rule written in this SKILL.md,
  **the skill-context rule wins** (more specific context takes priority вЂ” same principle as nested CLAUDE.md files)
- When there is no conflict, apply both: general rules from SKILL.md + project rules from skill-context
- Do NOT ignore skill-context rules even if they seem to contradict this skill's defaults вЂ”
  they exist because the project's experience proved the default insufficient
- **CRITICAL:** skill-context rules apply to ALL outputs of this skill вЂ” including the
  recommendations, examples, and checklists you present. If a skill-context rule says "best practices
  MUST prioritize X" or "examples MUST follow convention Y" вЂ” you MUST comply. Presenting guidance
  that contradicts skill-context rules is a bug.

**Enforcement:** After generating any output artifact, verify it against all skill-context rules.
If any rule is violated вЂ” fix the output before presenting it to the user.

## Quick Reference

- `$aif-best-practices` вЂ” Full overview
- `$aif-best-practices naming` вЂ” Naming conventions
- `$aif-best-practices structure` вЂ” Code organization
- `$aif-best-practices errors` вЂ” Error handling
- `$aif-best-practices testing` вЂ” Testing practices
- `$aif-best-practices review` вЂ” Code review checklist

---

## Naming Conventions

### Variables & Functions
```
вњ… Good                          вќЊ Bad
в”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђ
getUserById(id)                  getUser(i)
isValidEmail                     checkEmail
maxRetryCount                    max
calculateTotalPrice              calc
handleSubmit                     submit
```

**Rules:**
- Use descriptive names that reveal intent
- Avoid abbreviations (except universally known: `id`, `url`, `api`)
- Boolean variables: `is`, `has`, `can`, `should` prefix
- Functions: verb + noun (`fetchUser`, `validateInput`)
- Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
- Classes/Types: PascalCase
- Variables/functions: camelCase (JS/TS/PHP) or snake_case (Python/Rust)

### Files & Directories
```
вњ… Good                          вќЊ Bad
в”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђ
user-service.ts                  userService.ts (inconsistent)
UserRepository.ts                user_repository.ts (mixed)
/components/Button/              /Components/button/
/services/auth/                  /Services/Auth/
```

**Rules:**
- One convention per project (kebab-case or PascalCase for files)
- Directories: lowercase with hyphens
- Test files: `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` (consistent)
- Index files: only for re-exports, not logic

---

## Code Structure

### Function Design
```typescript
// вњ… Good: Single responsibility, clear inputs/outputs
function calculateDiscount(price: number, discountPercent: number): number {
  if (discountPercent < 0 || discountPercent > 100) {
    throw new Error('Discount must be between 0 and 100');
  }
  return price * (1 - discountPercent / 100);
}

// вќЊ Bad: Multiple responsibilities, side effects
function processOrder(order) {
  validateOrder(order);           // validation
  order.discount = getDiscount(); // mutation
  saveToDatabase(order);          // persistence
  sendEmail(order.user);          // notification
  return order;
}
```

```php
// вњ… Good: PHP with type declarations
function calculateDiscount(float $price, float $discountPercent): float
{
    if ($discountPercent < 0 || $discountPercent > 100) {
        throw new InvalidArgumentException('Discount must be between 0 and 100');
    }
    return $price * (1 - $discountPercent / 100);
}
```

**Rules:**
- Single Responsibility: one function = one job
- Max 20-30 lines per function
- Max 3-4 parameters (use object for more)
- No side effects in pure functions
- Early returns for guard clauses

### Module Organization
```
feature/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ index.ts          # Public exports only
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ types.ts          # Types and interfaces
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ constants.ts      # Constants
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ utils.ts          # Pure utility functions
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ hooks.ts          # React hooks (if applicable)
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ service.ts        # Business logic
в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository.ts     # Data access
```

**Rules:**
- Group by feature, not by type
- Clear public API via index.ts
- Internal modules prefixed with `_` or in `internal/`
- Avoid circular dependencies

---

## Error Handling

### Do's and Don'ts
```typescript
// вњ… Good: Specific errors, meaningful messages
class UserNotFoundError extends Error {
  constructor(userId: string) {
    super(`User not found: ${userId}`);
    this.name = 'UserNotFoundError';
  }
}

async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
  const user = await db.users.find(id);
  if (!user) {
    throw new UserNotFoundError(id);
  }
  return user;
}

// вќЊ Bad: Generic errors, swallowed exceptions
async function getUser(id) {
  try {
    return await db.users.find(id);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(e);  // Swallowed!
    return null;     // Hides the problem
  }
}
```

**Rules:**
- Create specific error classes for domain errors
- Never swallow exceptions without logging
- Log errors with context (user ID, request ID, etc.)
- Use error boundaries at system edges
- Return Result types for expected failures (optional)

### Error Messages
```
вњ… Good: "Failed to create user: email 'test@example.com' already exists"
вќЊ Bad: "Error occurred"
вќЊ Bad: "Something went wrong"
```

---

## Testing Practices

### Test Structure (AAA Pattern)
```typescript
describe('calculateDiscount', () => {
  it('should apply percentage discount to price', () => {
    // Arrange
    const price = 100;
    const discount = 20;

    // Act
    const result = calculateDiscount(price, discount);

    // Assert
    expect(result).toBe(80);
  });

  it('should throw for invalid discount percentage', () => {
    expect(() => calculateDiscount(100, -10)).toThrow();
    expect(() => calculateDiscount(100, 150)).toThrow();
  });
});
```

**Rules:**
- One assertion concept per test
- Descriptive test names: "should [expected behavior] when [condition]"
- Test behavior, not implementation
- Use factories/fixtures for test data
- Avoid testing private methods directly

### Test Coverage Priorities
```
1. Critical business logic      в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€ Must have
2. Edge cases and boundaries    в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Important
3. Integration points           в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Important
4. Happy paths                  в–€в–€в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Basic
5. UI components                в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Optional
```

---

## Code Review Checklist

### Before Requesting Review
- [ ] Self-reviewed the diff
- [ ] Tests pass locally
- [ ] No debug code (console.log, debugger)
- [ ] No commented-out code
- [ ] Updated documentation if needed
- [ ] Commit messages are clear

### Reviewer Checklist
- [ ] **Correctness**: Does it do what it claims?
- [ ] **Edge cases**: What could go wrong?
- [ ] **Security**: Any vulnerabilities? (see `$aif-security-checklist`)
- [ ] **Performance**: Any obvious bottlenecks?
- [ ] **Readability**: Can I understand it in 5 minutes?
- [ ] **Tests**: Are critical paths covered?
- [ ] **Consistency**: Follows project conventions?

### Review Comments
```
вњ… Good feedback:
"This could throw if `user` is null. Consider adding a null check
or using optional chaining: `user?.profile?.name`"

вќЊ Bad feedback:
"This is wrong"
"I don't like this"
"Why did you do it this way?"
```

---

## Quick Rules Summary

| Area | Rule |
|------|------|
| Naming | Descriptive, consistent, reveals intent |
| Functions | Small, single purpose, no side effects |
| Errors | Specific types, never swallow, log context |
| Tests | AAA pattern, test behavior, descriptive names |
| Reviews | Be specific, suggest solutions, be kind |

## Artifact Ownership and Config Policy

- Primary ownership: none. This skill is advisory and reference-only.
- Write policy: do not create or modify project artifacts by default.
- Config policy: config-agnostic by design. Follow repository context, `.ai-factory/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and skill-context overrides instead of reading `config.yaml`.
# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text в‰Ґ4.5:1, large text в‰Ґ3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65вЂ“75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12вЂ“16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

### Step 0.2: Find Plan Artifact

Normalize every selected artifact to:

- `plan_entrypoint` вЂ” the single markdown file containing settings and `## Tasks`
- `plan_bundle_dir` вЂ” empty for fast/full/fix plans; the ultra directory otherwise
- `phase_files` вЂ” empty for single-file plans; ordered links from the ultra

```
2. If no branch artifact resolves, count active named artifacts as:
```

# Logging Requirements

**ALWAYS add verbose logging when implementing code.** AI-generated code often has subtle bugs that are hard to debug without proper logging.

## Logging Guidelines

1. **Log function entry/exit** with parameters and return values
2. **Log state changes** - before and after mutations
3. **Log external calls** - API requests, database queries, file operations
4. **Log error context** - include relevant variables, not just error message
5. **Use structured logging** when possible (JSON format)

## Example Pattern

```typescript
function processOrder(order: Order): Result {
  console.log('[processOrder] START', { orderId: order.id, items: order.items.length });

  try {
    const validated = validateOrder(order);
    console.log('[processOrder] Validation passed', { validated });

    const result = submitToPayment(validated);
    console.log('[processOrder] Payment result', { success: result.success, transactionId: result.id });

    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[processOrder] ERROR', { orderId: order.id, error: error.message, stack: error.stack });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Log Management Requirements

**Logs must be configurable and manageable:**

1. **Use log levels** - DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
2. **Environment-based control** - LOG_LEVEL env variable
3. **Easy to disable** - single flag or env var to turn off verbose logs
4. **Consider rotation** - for file-based logs, implement rotation or use existing tools

```typescript
// Good: Configurable logging
const LOG_LEVEL = process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'debug';
const logger = createLogger({ level: LOG_LEVEL });

// Good: Can be disabled
if (process.env.DEBUG) {
  console.log('[debug]', data);
}

// Bad: Hardcoded verbose logs that can't be turned off
console.log(hugeObject); // Will pollute production logs
```

## Why This Matters

- AI-generated code may have edge cases not covered
- Logs help identify WHERE things go wrong
- Debugging without logs wastes significant time
- User can remove logs later if needed, but missing logs during development is costly
- **Production safety** - logs must be reducible to avoid performance issues and storage costs

**DO NOT skip logging to "keep code clean" - verbose logging is REQUIRED during implementation, but MUST be configurable.**

# Logging Requirements

**ALWAYS add verbose logging when implementing code.** AI-generated code often has subtle bugs that are hard to debug without proper logging.

## Logging Guidelines

1. **Log function entry/exit** with parameters and return values
2. **Log state changes** - before and after mutations
3. **Log external calls** - API requests, database queries, file operations
4. **Log error context** - include relevant variables, not just error message
5. **Use structured logging** when possible (JSON format)

## Example Pattern

```typescript
function processOrder(order: Order): Result {
  console.log('[processOrder] START', { orderId: order.id, items: order.items.length });

  try {
    const validated = validateOrder(order);
    console.log('[processOrder] Validation passed', { validated });

    const result = submitToPayment(validated);
    console.log('[processOrder] Payment result', { success: result.success, transactionId: result.id });

    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[processOrder] ERROR', { orderId: order.id, error: error.message, stack: error.stack });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Log Management Requirements

**Logs must be configurable and manageable:**

1. **Use log levels** - DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
2. **Environment-based control** - LOG_LEVEL env variable
3. **Easy to disable** - single flag or env var to turn off verbose logs
4. **Consider rotation** - for file-based logs, implement rotation or use existing tools

```typescript
// Good: Configurable logging
const LOG_LEVEL = process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'debug';
const logger = createLogger({ level: LOG_LEVEL });

// Good: Can be disabled
if (process.env.DEBUG) {
  console.log('[debug]', data);
}

// Bad: Hardcoded verbose logs that can't be turned off
console.log(hugeObject); // Will pollute production logs
```

## Why This Matters

- AI-generated code may have edge cases not covered
- Logs help identify WHERE things go wrong
- Debugging without logs wastes significant time
- User can remove logs later if needed, but missing logs during development is costly
- **Production safety** - logs must be reducible to avoid performance issues and storage costs

**DO NOT skip logging to "keep code clean" - verbose logging is REQUIRED during implementation, but MUST be configurable.**

## Naming Conventions

### Variables & Functions
```
вњ… Good                          вќЊ Bad
в”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђ
getUserById(id)                  getUser(i)
isValidEmail                     checkEmail
maxRetryCount                    max
calculateTotalPrice              calc
handleSubmit                     submit
```

**Rules:**
- Use descriptive names that reveal intent
- Avoid abbreviations (except universally known: `id`, `url`, `api`)
- Boolean variables: `is`, `has`, `can`, `should` prefix
- Functions: verb + noun (`fetchUser`, `validateInput`)
- Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
- Classes/Types: PascalCase
- Variables/functions: camelCase (JS/TS/PHP) or snake_case (Python/Rust)

### Files & Directories
```
вњ… Good                          вќЊ Bad
в”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђв”Ђ

UserRepository.ts                user_repository.ts (mixed)
/components/Button/              /Components/button/
/services/auth/                  /Services/Auth/
```

**Rules:**
- One convention per project (kebab-case or PascalCase for files)
- Directories: lowercase with hyphens
- Test files: `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` (consistent)
- Index files: only for re-exports, not logic

---

## Code Structure

### Function Design
```typescript
// вњ… Good: Single responsibility, clear inputs/outputs
function calculateDiscount(price: number, discountPercent: number): number {
  if (discountPercent < 0 || discountPercent > 100) {
    throw new Error('Discount must be between 0 and 100');
  }
  return price * (1 - discountPercent / 100);
}

// вќЊ Bad: Multiple responsibilities, side effects
function processOrder(order) {
  validateOrder(order);           // validation
  order.discount = getDiscount(); // mutation
  saveToDatabase(order);          // persistence
  sendEmail(order.user);          // notification
  return order;
}
```

```php
// вњ… Good: PHP with type declarations
function calculateDiscount(float $price, float $discountPercent): float
{
    if ($discountPercent < 0 || $discountPercent > 100) {
        throw new InvalidArgumentException('Discount must be between 0 and 100');
    }
    return $price * (1 - $discountPercent / 100);
}
```

**Rules:**
- Single Responsibility: one function = one job
- Max 20-30 lines per function
- Max 3-4 parameters (use object for more)
- No side effects in pure functions
- Early returns for guard clauses

### Module Organization
```
feature/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ index.ts          # Public exports only
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ types.ts          # Types and interfaces
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ constants.ts      # Constants
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ utils.ts          # Pure utility functions
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ hooks.ts          # React hooks (if applicable)
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ service.ts        # Business logic
в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository.ts     # Data access
```

**Rules:**
- Group by feature, not by type
- Clear public API via index.ts
- Internal modules prefixed with `_` or in `internal/`
- Avoid circular dependencies

---

## Error Handling

### Do's and Don'ts
```typescript
// вњ… Good: Specific errors, meaningful messages
class UserNotFoundError extends Error {
  constructor(userId: string) {
    super(`User not found: ${userId}`);
    this.name = 'UserNotFoundError';
  }
}

async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
  const user = await db.users.find(id);
  if (!user) {
    throw new UserNotFoundError(id);
  }
  return user;
}

// вќЊ Bad: Generic errors, swallowed exceptions
async function getUser(id) {
  try {
    return await db.users.find(id);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(e);  // Swallowed!
    return null;     // Hides the problem
  }
}
```

**Rules:**
- Create specific error classes for domain errors
- Never swallow exceptions without logging
- Log errors with context (user ID, request ID, etc.)
- Use error boundaries at system edges
- Return Result types for expected failures (optional)

### Error Messages
```
вњ… Good: "Failed to create user: email 'test@example.com' already exists"
вќЊ Bad: "Error occurred"
вќЊ Bad: "Something went wrong"
```

---

## Testing Practices

### Test Structure (AAA Pattern)
```typescript
describe('calculateDiscount', () => {
  it('should apply percentage discount to price', () => {
    // Arrange
    const price = 100;
    const discount = 20;

    // Act
    const result = calculateDiscount(price, discount);

    // Assert
    expect(result).toBe(80);
  });

  it('should throw for invalid discount percentage', () => {
    expect(() => calculateDiscount(100, -10)).toThrow();
    expect(() => calculateDiscount(100, 150)).toThrow();
  });
});
```

**Rules:**
- One assertion concept per test
- Descriptive test names: "should [expected behavior] when [condition]"
- Test behavior, not implementation
- Use factories/fixtures for test data
- Avoid testing private methods directly

### Test Coverage Priorities
```
1. Critical business logic      в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€ Must have
2. Edge cases and boundaries    в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Important
3. Integration points           в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Important
4. Happy paths                  в–€в–€в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Basic
5. UI components                в–€в–€в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘в–‘ Optional
```

## Code Review Checklist

### Before Requesting Review
- [ ] Self-reviewed the diff
- [ ] Tests pass locally
- [ ] No debug code (console.log, debugger)
- [ ] No commented-out code
- [ ] Updated documentation if needed

### Reviewer Checklist

- [ ] **Edge cases**: What could go wrong?
- [ ] **Security**: Any vulnerabilities? (see `$aif-security-checklist`)
- [ ] **Performance**: Any obvious bottlenecks?
- [ ] **Readability**: Can I understand it in 5 minutes?
- [ ] **Tests**: Are critical paths covered?
- [ ] **Consistency**: Follows project conventions?

### Review Comments
```
вњ… Good feedback:
"This could throw if `user` is null. Consider adding a null check
or using optional chaining: `user?.profile?.name`"

вќЊ Bad feedback:
"This is wrong"
"I don't like this"

```

---

## Quick Rules Summary

| Area | Rule |
|------|------|
| Naming | Descriptive, consistent, reveals intent |
| Functions | Small, single purpose, no side effects |
| Errors | Specific types, never swallow, log context |
| Tests | AAA pattern, test behavior, descriptive names |
| Reviews | Be specific, suggest solutions, be kind |

## Artifact Ownership and Config Policy

- Primary ownership: none. This skill is advisory and reference-only.
- Write policy: do not create or modify project artifacts by default.
- Config policy: config-agnostic by design. Follow repository context, `.ai-factory/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and skill-context overrides instead of reading `config.yaml`.
# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text в‰Ґ4.5:1, large text в‰Ґ3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65вЂ“75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12вЂ“16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
